fixed_cases: All twenty existing original Float32 65x65 windows, without selecting winners or expanding/altering source windows.
selection: For each family, minimum whole-domain E2 under fixed complete GPR4 byte ceiling; separately minimum complete file satisfying guarded continuous source-relative maximum-error target. Ties resolve by bytes, E2, nx, ny. Every grid and all losses retained. This is a finite tensor-grid candidate comparison, not a paper-style P1 algorithm or global optimal encoding.
hybrid: On every tensor rectangle, choose the lower whole-cell L2-squared residual of bilinear ruled and two antidiagonal P1 triangles, with ruled as exact tie choice. Adjacent same-family runs share row band/triangle-strip records. All metadata and split-run overhead count in real files. Cell choice minimizes E2 at this grid, not maximum error or total file bytes.
continuity: One global integer tensor grid; all cells pass through shared corner nodes and have the same linear edge functions. Ruled and P1 may meet without T junctions and are C0 in real arithmetic. Gradient is one-sided and may jump; no C1 claim.
metrics: Source is the exact original-node bilinear function, not surveyed ground. Ruled residual on each 1m source cell is bilinear, maximum at a source-cell corner; P1 residual is bilinear minus plane, with interior saddles and linear axis edges. Also check extrema on every clipped antidiagonal segment. Whole E2 uses exact bilinear mass matrices, with degree-exact three-node Gauss-Duffy on diagonal cuts; independent five-node release integrals. Float64 guard, not interval proof.
reporting: All 20 x 49 x 3 = 2940 native candidates, 200 byte pairs and 120 maximum-target selections. Shared georeferenced GPR4 header and point pool, no source-precision rounding. Existing paper, P2, raster and negative controls remain. No ArcGIS software/CPU/GPU/RAM superiority claim.
